purpose: Research, version, validate, approve and reuse subject identity/persona/world profiles inside the existing KALP Cinematic Studio.

gates.pass_condition: Subject and creative intent are resolved.
Research records contain source URLs, retrieved-at timestamps, evidence summaries and uncertainty labels.
Required identity, persona, communication, knowledge, world and production fields are populated.
Schema, source coverage, identity consistency and safety checks pass.
First profile version or major change is explicitly approved.
Versioned profile is saved to canonical storage and read back successfully; Excel export is a human-readable mirror.
Topic, audience, language, reel count and frame count are resolved.
Requested frame count is exact; for the default three-reel format this is 3 reels × 8 frames = 24 frames.
Character/world/story continuity and renderer schema validate before production handoff.

persistence.canonical_store: Existing application persistence layer, after capability audit; do not treat browser localStorage or GitHub source files as cross-user durable memory.
persistence.excel_role: Exportable human-readable mirror with Profile, DNA, Sources, Validation and Version History sheets.
persistence.versioning: Immutable approved versions; proposed changes never overwrite the active approved version.

adapters.character_registry: Extend existing apps/cinematic-studio/data/character-registry.json contracts without replacing the registry.
adapters.retro64: Reuse apps/cinematic-studio/retro64-ui-v2.js and its Excel/reference-driven DNA logic as the first domain adapter.
adapters.scene_runtime: Reuse apps/cinematic-studio/api/cinematic.js scene/frame contracts where compatible.
adapters.renderer: Reuse existing storyboard and production handoff; no parallel storyboard engine.

known_gaps: The existing cinematic runtime currently generates an 8-frame scene from a registered character selection; it is not yet a universal 24-frame discourse engine.
The visible MCP/Gemini/Governor selector in index.html is UI state and is not, by itself, proof of a connected automatic research provider.
The current cinematic API reads JSON contracts and generates scene data; it does not provide durable profile CRUD or human-approval persistence.
Retro 64 has its own workbook-driven reference ingestion and 3-reel progression logic, but its selected-game workflow is domain-specific.
